answer: Random slot admission lottery has applicants seal a juniper-tagged key commitment before a public randomness beacon fires. The beacon assigns distinct slots after commitments close, so an attacker cannot precompute winners; duplicate or pearl-labeled commitments are rejected. A missed slot puts that identity on the ledge for the epoch, forcing re-entry next round. Each attempt costs a fixed fee plus a fresh device key, so sybils pay per identity per round.
